prompt: Print jobs come out in the order they were sent.
tells: in the order they were sent
why: The first job sent is the first one printed, and later jobs wait their turn. First in, first out is a queue.
trap: No job jumps ahead, so it isn't a priority queue.

prompt: A support line answers callers first come, first served.
why: Callers are answered in the order they called. First come, first served is a queue.

prompt: A ticket website lets people in from the waiting room in arrival order.
why: People are let in in the order they arrived, with no skipping ahead. Serving by arrival order is a queue.

prompt: Breadth-first search visits all neighbours one step away before going two steps away.
why: BFS adds neighbours to the back and takes from the front, so everyone one step away comes out before anyone two steps away. That level order comes from a queue.
trap: The data is a graph, but the visiting order comes from a queue.

prompt: Messages between two services are handled oldest first, so none jump the line.
why: The oldest message is handled first and nothing jumps ahead. Handling items in arrival order is a queue.
trap: Newest first would be a stack.

prompt: A music app's Up Next list plays songs in the order you added them.
tells: in the order you added them
why: The song you added first plays first, and new songs go to the end. Added first, played first is a queue.
trap: A stack would play your latest addition first.
